title: Crop Diversity Subindex
text: SHMI Diversity subindex quantifies diversity crops grown across entire rotation, accounting species identity time field. Diversity computed using entropy‑based Hill numbers, generalize richness, Shannon entropy, Simpson entropy unified framework. algorithm expands crop mixtures, sums plant‑days across years rotation, computes species proportions, applies selected Hill‑number order (default: Simpson entropy, q=2q = 2). final score scaled 0–100 using user‑specified theoretical maximum (default: max_div = 8).

title: Build SHMI Scores from Prepared Inputs — build_shmi
text: Cover — season‑weighted plant presence Diversity — rotation‑scale crop diversity (Hill numbers) Inverse disturbance — EPA mechanistic STIR method Organic inputs — amendments + animal integration default, SHMI computed using official national settings (“locked mode”). expert mode, users may override setting, resulting SHMI values longer comparable national SHMI scale. ## Required inputs function expects list returned prepare_shmi_inputs() : rot_bounds — rotation start/end dates rotation years crop — harmonized crop windows (one row per species) dist — disturbance events (EPA/STIR inputs) amend — amendment events animal — animal integration events mgt — management metadata (study, farm, field, treatment) ## Disturbance method Disturbance can computed using: "EPA" — mechanistic soil‑mixing model (profile penetration) "STIR" — daily summed mixing efficiency (SD_mixeff) methods classify annual tillage intensity using modified Tier‑3 Z–K scheme compute inverse disturbance 0–100 scale. ## Settings expert mode locked mode (expert_mode = FALSE), SHMI uses official national settings: seasonal cover weights Hill‑number order maximum diversity STIR normalization constant amendment/animal weights pillar weights SHMI aggregation expert mode, user‑supplied settings override defaults. Missing settings filled official values. ## SHMI computation workflow Settings: locked mode vs expert mode. Input validation: structural checks required inputs. Pillar computation: Cover — compute_cover() Diversity — compute_diversity() Inverse disturbance — compute_disturbance() Organic inputs — compute_orginput() Weighted combination:     Pillar scores normalized weights sum 1, combined: $$       SHMI =         w_{cover} \cdot Cover +         w_{div}   \cdot Diversity +         w_{dist}  \cdot InvDist +         w_{ani}   \cdot OrgInput     $$ Output assembly:     Returns tidy data frame SHMI scores metadata describing     settings used, SHMI version, computation timestamp.

title: Compute the SHMI Cover Sub‑index (Season‑Weighted Plant Presence) — compute_cover
text: ## Mixture‑aware cover windows input `crop` table contains one row per crop species. Mixtures therefore appear multiple rows identical `CD_seq_num` values. cover scoring, mixtures must treated *single* planting event. function collapses mixtures grouping : MGT_combo CD_seq_num computing: earliest crop_start latest   crop_end produces one cover window per planting event, regardless mixture complexity. ## Daily plant‑presence expansion cover window expanded daily records. day assigned season based calendar month: Winter: December–February Spring: March–May Summer: June–August Fall:   September–November Seasonal plant‑days counted management unit. ## Rotation‑based normalization Rotation bounds (`rot_start`, `rot_end`) expanded daily records compute number *possible* days season. Seasonal cover proportion : $$   p_{season} = \frac{\text{plant-days}}{\text{possible-days}} $$ Seasons zero possible days contribute zero. ## Seasonal weighting scaling Seasonal proportions combined using user‑specified weights: w_winter w_spring w_summer w_fall Weights normalized sum 1. final cover score : $$   \text{Cover} = 100 \times \sum_{season} w_{season} \, p_{season} $$ yielding value [0, 100].

title: Compute Inverse Disturbance Using EPA Mechanistic or STIR Methods — compute_disturbance
text: **EPA mechanistic soil-mixing model** (profile penetration–based), **STIR disturbance intensity** (daily summed mixing efficiency). methods produce annual tillage-intensity (TI) value rotation year. Annual TI values classified **modified Tier 3 tillage-intensity scheme (Z–K)** derived EPA Soil-Mixing Report. ## Modified Tier 3 Classification (Z–K) published Tier 3 ranges (–K) contain gaps include zero-disturbance class. ensure complete coverage [0, 1] domain: new class **Z** added TI = 0. class boundaries converted **closed–open intervals**         (e.g., [0.01, 0.04)), ensuring TI maps exactly one class. midpoint class Z explicitly set **0**. annual TI replaced midpoint class: $$ T_{t}^{mid} = (TI_{min} + TI_{max}) / 2 $$ T_{t}^{mid} = 0 class Z. inverse-disturbance score rescales midpoints : **0 disturbance → 100**, **midpoint class K → 0**. $$   T_{t}^{inv} = 100 \times \left(1 - \frac{T_{t}^{mid}}{T_{K}^{mid}}\right) $$ Rotation-level disturbance mean annual inverse-disturbance values. Units disturbance events receive score 100. ## EPA Mechanistic Method EPA method computes mechanistic profile penetration tillage pass using mixing efficiency tillage depth. Passes occurring date treated sequential operations, producing *daily* TI value. Daily TI values summed annual TI. Required columns `dist`: MGT_combo — management unit identifier SD_date — date tillage pass SD_mixeff — mixing efficiency (0–1) SD_depth — tillage depth (inches; converted internally) ## STIR Method STIR method computes daily disturbance intensity : $$ SDsum = \sum SD\_mixeff $$ summed across passes given date. Annual STIR sum daily SDsum values. Annual STIR normalized TI = STIR\_raw / max\_stir classified using Z–K scheme. Required columns `dist`: MGT_combo SD_date SD_mixeff ## Rotation Bounds data frame containing rotation-year boundaries: MGT_combo rot_start rot_end rot_start_yr rot_end_yr

title: Compute Rotation‑Scale Crop Diversity (Entropy‑Based Hill Numbers) — compute_diversity
text: ## Mixture expansion input `crop` table contains one row per crop species. Mixtures therefore appear single rows whose `CD_name` contains multiple species (e.g., `"+ B + C"`) placeholder mixture names (e.g., `"8-species"`). Mixtures expanded individual species using: splitting real mixtures `"+"`, expanding placeholder mixtures synthetic species         (`species_1`, `species_2`, …). species inherits `crop_start` `crop_end` interval. ## Rotation‑scale plant‑days species, plant‑days computed : $$   \text{days} = (\text{crop\_end} - \text{crop\_start}) + 1 $$ Plant‑days summed across years rotation. Fallow contributes zero plant‑days. ## Hill‑number diversity Species proportions : $$   p_i = \frac{\text{days}_i}{\sum_j \text{days}_j} $$ Diversity computed using Hill‑number entropy metrics: Richness: \(D = \sum (p_i > 0)\) Shannon entropy: \(D = -\sum p_i \log p_i\) Simpson entropy (entropy form): \(D = -\log \sum p_i^2\) diversity value capped max_div scaled 0–100: Richness: \(D / max\_div\) Entropy metrics: \(D / \log(max\_div)\)

title: Compute the Organic Inputs Sub-index (Amendments + Animals) — compute_orginput
text: algorithm proceeds five steps: Rotation-year grid:     Construct sequence rotation years MGT_combo. Amendment presence:     Identify rotation years organic amendments mark     amend_present = 1. Animal presence:     Identify rotation years animal events mark     ani_present = 1. Binary organic-input presence:     rotation year receives org_present = 1 either     amend_present == 1 w_amend > 0,     ani_present == 1 w_animal > 0.     Multiple events within year increase score. Final score:     organic-inputs indicator returned     $$ \mathrm{OrgInputs} = 100 \times \mathrm{mean}(org\_present) $$     representing percentage rotation years organic inputs.     Units organic inputs receive score 0.
